kunyah: Abu Abd ar-Rahman — Ibn Umm Abd
tribe: Hudhayl — allies of Banu Zuhra of Quraysh
era: The Reciter of the Prophet's ﷺ Household
teaser: A shepherd boy guarding another man's sheep. The Prophet ﷺ told the ummah to take the Qur'an from him.
quran_mention: «الرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ» — 'The Merciful. He taught the Qur'an' — Quran 55:1-2, the surah he recited aloud to Quraysh

layers.title: Who
layers.subtitle: So small they laughed at his legs
layers.content:
He was 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ibn Ghafil, of Hudhayl. His people were not Quraysh; his father had made an alliance with 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith of the Banu Zuhra, which is how the family came to live in Makka at all. His mother was Umm 'Abd, and half the reports call him not by his father's name but by hers: Ibn Umm 'Abd. His kunya was Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman.

He was small. Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who saw him, said simply: 'a thin man with little flesh.' Others describe him as short and very dark-skinned, with hair that reached his collarbone which he tucked behind his ears when he went into sajdah. He did not use henna. His ring was iron. He wore white and he wore the best scent in Madina — Talha said he could be recognised at night by the smell of his perfume.

Once the Prophet ﷺ told him to climb a tree and fetch something down. The men watching laughed at how thin his legs were. The Prophet ﷺ asked what they were laughing at, and then said: 'The foot of 'Abdullah will be heavier than Uhud in the balance on the Day of Rising.'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ: 'They will be heavier in the balance than Uhud' — narrated from Zirr ibn Hubaysh and from 'Ali, in Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: The boy who would not give away what was not his
layers.content:
He told the story himself. 'I was a young boy herding sheep for 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt when the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr came, fleeing from the idolaters. They said, Boy, do you have any milk we can drink?' He answered that the flock was a trust in his hands and he was not their cupbearer. He would not give away another man's property, not even to these two.

The Prophet ﷺ asked whether he had a young sheep that had never been mated. He brought it. The Prophet ﷺ hobbled it, stroked the udder, made supplication, and the udder flowed. Abu Bakr brought a hollow stone and milked into it. Abu Bakr drank, then the boy drank. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to the udder, 'Contract,' and it did.

The boy came back afterwards and said: 'Teach me some of these words.' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'You are a boy who learns.' 'So I learned seventy suras from his mouth,' he said, 'and no one contends with me about them.'

He became Muslim before the Prophet ﷺ had even entered the house of al-Arqam. He was among the very first.
layers.hadith_ref: The account of the milk and 'You are a boy who learns' — narrated by 'Affan ibn Muslim from Hammad ibn Salama from 'Asim from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, in Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: Sandals, pillow, toothstick — and the whole Qur'an
layers.content:
Nobody had recited the Qur'an aloud to Quraysh in their own gathering place. Ibn Mas'ud volunteered. He stood at the Maqam and recited Surat ar-Rahman until they struck his face. Ibn Sa'd puts the same fact plainly: 'The first to disseminate the Qur'an in Makka from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.'

In Madina he became something closer than a companion. He carried the Prophet's ﷺ sandals, his pillow, his toothstick and his water for purification on journeys. He screened him when he washed, woke him when he slept, walked ahead of him with his staff. The Prophet ﷺ told him: 'You can listen to me if the curtain is raised and you can hear my secrets until I forbid you.' Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said, 'I saw the Prophet ﷺ, and I only saw Ibn Mas'ud as part of his family.'

At Badr he struck the neck of Abu Jahl after the sons of 'Afra' had brought him down. And the Prophet ﷺ named him first when he told the community where to learn: 'Take the Qur'an from four' — and the first of the four was 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an — 'Take the Qur'an from four', narrated by 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr; the Prophet's ﷺ words about the raised curtain are in Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley; Ibn Hisham, as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah, for the recitation at the Maqam

layers.title: The Trial and Quality
layers.subtitle: He was afraid to say 'the Prophet ﷺ said'
layers.content:
Here is the strange thing about the man who knew the most. He almost never narrated.

'Amr ibn Maymun said: 'I frequented 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud for a year and did not hear him relate anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — except that one day he started to relate a hadith and said, The Messenger of Allah said... Grief came over him until I saw sweat flowing from his brow. Then he said: If Allah wills, either above that, or close to that, or less than that.'

'Alqama said he sat with him every Thursday evening for years and heard him say 'The Messenger of Allah said' on one single occasion — and as he said it, the staff he was leaning on shook in his hand.

This was his trial and his quality at once. He held the words of the Prophet ﷺ as a trust, exactly as he had once held another man's sheep, and he would not hand over a syllable he was not certain of. Hudhayfa said the man closest to the Prophet ﷺ in guidance and manner, from the moment he left his house until he returned to it, was Ibn Umm 'Abd. 'Umar looked at him crossing a room and said three times: 'A bag filled with knowledge.'
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley — narrated from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Alqama ibn Qays, from Hudhayfa, and from Zayd ibn Wahb

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: 'Umar gave Kufa the thing he wanted for himself
layers.content:
'Umar found him at Homs and sent him to Kufa instead, writing to its people: 'By Allah, I have preferred you with him over myself. Take him.' A caliph gave away the teacher he wanted for his own city. Out of that decision came the school of Kufa, and out of Kufa came much of what later generations know of the Qur'an's recitation and of fiqh.

He died in Madina in 32 AH, around sixty years old. He was buried at night, at al-Baqi', in the ground he had asked for — beside 'Uthman ibn Maz'un. Reports differ over who led the prayer; Ibn Sa'd holds it firmest that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan did, though some said 'Ammar ibn Yasir. He left ninety thousand dirhams and had instructed that his own shroud cost two hundred.

Abu Musa and Abu Mas'ud stood together after the burial. One said to the other: 'Do you think anyone like him will be left after him?'

When you recite the Qur'an today, part of what you are holding came down a chain that runs through the mouth of a small dark-skinned shepherd whose legs were laughed at.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley — 'Umar's letter narrated from 'Amir; the death and burial from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utba and Qatada

quiz.prompt: What work was Ibn Mas'ud doing when he first met the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: He was a blacksmith in Makka
He was herding sheep for 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt
He was a scribe for the Quraysh
He was a water-carrier at the Ka'bah

quiz.citation: Narrated from Zirr ibn Hubaysh — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The flock was not his. When two strangers asked him for milk, he refused because the sheep were a trust in his hands. He was tested on amanah before he was ever taught a single ayah.

quiz.prompt: How many suras did Ibn Mas'ud say he learned directly from the mouth of the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: Forty
Fifty
Seventy
The entire Qur'an

quiz.citation: His own words, narrated from Zirr ibn Hubaysh — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'I learned seventy suras from his mouth, and no one contends with me about them.' Not copied from a page. Taken from a mouth, one at a time, by a boy who had asked to be taught.

quiz.prompt: According to Ibn Sa'd, what was Ibn Mas'ud the first to do in Makka?

options.text: Pray openly at the Ka'bah
Break an idol of Quraysh
Disseminate the Qur'an aloud from the mouth of the Prophet ﷺ
Write down the revelation

quiz.citation: Al-Qasim ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III; the incident at the Maqam is in Ibn Hisham, as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah
quiz.scholar_reflection: He was among the physically weakest and socially smallest of them, and he was the one who went and said it out loud where Quraysh gathered. They struck his face for it.

quiz.prompt: 'Amr ibn Maymun sat with Ibn Mas'ud for a whole year. How many hadith did he hear him narrate in that time?

options.text: Hundreds — he narrated constantly
One, and Ibn Mas'ud broke into sweat as he said it
None at all
Only what he wrote down and read out

quiz.citation: Narrated from Muslim al-Batin from 'Amr ibn Maymun — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He added, 'If Allah wills, either above that, or close to that, or less than that.' He would not claim the exact wording. The man who knew the most was the most careful about the little he said.

quiz.prompt: What did 'Umar write to the people of Kufa when he sent Ibn Mas'ud to them?

options.text: 'Obey him in everything'
'He is your governor, not your teacher'
'By Allah, I have preferred you with him over myself. Take him.'
'Return him to me after one year'

quiz.citation: Narrated from Dawud from 'Amir — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Kufa became one of the great centres of Qur'anic learning because a caliph gave away the man he most wanted near him. Some legacies are built by the person who lets go.

quiz.prompt: As a boy he refused to give away milk that was not his, even to the Prophet ﷺ. When have you had to hold a line about something entrusted to you?

options.text: I hold it strictly, even when it makes me look difficult
I bend when the person asking clearly deserves better
I am stricter with other people's things than with my own
I have given things away I had no right to give

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account narrated from Zirr ibn Hubaysh — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He did not know who was standing in front of him. That is what makes the refusal worth something — it was not calculated, it was just how he was.

quiz.prompt: Men laughed at how thin his legs were. The Prophet ﷺ answered that those legs would outweigh Uhud. What do you do with the parts of yourself that get laughed at?
quiz.slider_label: What others find small in you

options.text: I hide them and route around them
I joke about them first so nobody else gets to
I have stopped negotiating about them
They still sting, and I am not pretending otherwise

quiz.citation: Reflection on the incident narrated from 'Ali and from Zirr ibn Hubaysh
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ did not tell them to stop noticing. He told them what the scales would say. The measurement they were using was simply the wrong one.

quiz.prompt: He held the Prophet's ﷺ words so carefully that he would rather say nothing than risk a wrong word. Where do you sit between speaking freely and speaking exactly?

options.text: I would rather say less and be sure of it
I would rather share what I have and let others correct me
It depends entirely on whether I am quoting someone else
I speak more confidently than my actual knowledge allows

quiz.citation: Reflection on the reports of 'Amr ibn Maymun and 'Alqama ibn Qays
quiz.scholar_reflection: The whole science of hadith transmission grew out of instincts like his. Sweat on the brow of a man about to quote is not anxiety. It is weight, correctly felt.

quiz.prompt: Hudhayfa said Ibn Mas'ud was the closest to the Prophet ﷺ in manner from the moment he left home until he came back — and admitted he could not speak for what he was like inside his own house. What does that distinction raise for you?
quiz.slider_label: The version of you at home

options.text: My family gets the truer version, for better or worse
My family gets the tired version, and that is not the same as the true one
There is less gap than there used to be
I would rather not audit that too closely right now

quiz.citation: Narrated from Shaqiq and from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Another report answers the question anyway: when 'Abdullah came into his house he was sociable and raised his voice so that his family would be at ease. He was easier at home, not harder.

quiz.prompt: He left ninety thousand dirhams, and instructed that his own burial shroud cost two hundred. What is your reaction to that ratio?
quiz.slider_label: What you spend on yourself last

options.text: It is the clearest sign of where he thought the money belonged
It suggests he never really considered the wealth his
It reads to me as a last instruction to his children
I notice I would find that difficult to do

quiz.citation: Narrated from Zirr ibn Hubaysh and from Khaytham ibn 'Amr — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He was described as one of the most generous of people, who wore white and the finest scent in Madina. He was not against enjoying provision. He simply knew which part of it he was taking with him.
